field: B3 (Wikipedia: 'There have been instances of books being stripped of attribution to the project and sold for profit in the Kindle Store and other booksellers'; 'There is no legal impediment to the reselling of works in the public domain if all references to Project Gutenberg are removed'). classes.term: the undocumented edition of a transcription (which version of a text was digitized)
classes.basis: field: B3 (Wikipedia: 'In December 1994, Project Gutenberg was criticized by the Text Encoding Initiative for ... not documenting which of several (conflicting) versions of a text has been the one digitized.'). classes_note: Four classes, each sourced by the field and the census record: (1) digital libraries of public-domain texts whose texts enter training corpora (B3, B7; census area 'corpora', evidence_kind, record.in_layer); (2) machine-made works composed from a library's texts (B1's Open Audiobook Collection, B8 NaNoGenMo; census record.makes); (3) attribution stripped from redistributed texts (B3; census record.name, does_not_answer); (4) the undocumented edition of a transcription (B3's TEI criticism; census negative_tags, does_not_answer). The aliases are the entity's name, its German sister's name (a distinct entity: candidates read and kept apart), its host, the Pile's PG-19 component (a distinct entity, read for what it says of the library) and the bare name 'Gutenberg', which the archive uses for the library ('Gutenberg's texts', 'the Gutenberg text'), its uses for the printer, the press and the print era excluded where the phrase names them; the reading removes the rest (Johannes Gutenberg, the press). #186 and #1543, the census's anchors, are read at the passages on corpora, the address to the training layer, persistence and attribution, and machine composition. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the entity and says something of it (a description, a use, a limit, a corrective); R where it states a relation between the entity and an archive object (the archive's Originals Library and its seatings drawn from the library); O-class where a sentence applies an archive category to one of the four classes; a bare mention, a bibliography line or a catalogue row is not a claim.
